Argentina thrashed Costa Rica 7-0 in an international friendly on Tuesday, with Nico Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono scoring twice each. Paz opened the scoring in the eighth minute, converting Enzo Fernandez’s assist to put Argentina ahead at the start of the contest. Julian Alvarez doubled the lead in the 35th minute after being set up by Agustin Giay, before Paz scored his second three minutes later from Maximo Perrone’s pass. Alvarez added his second goal in the 43rd minute, finishing a move created by Gianluca Prestianni to give Argentina a commanding 4-0 lead at half-time. Argentina continued their dominance after the break, with Mastantuono coming off the bench to score in the 48th minute following an assist from Perrone. Argentina lose 2-1 to Uruguay in first post-Messi match Argentina appeals FIFA sanctions over World Cup final Argentina leave Messi’s No. 10 vacant for friendlies Alexis Mac Allister made it 6-0 in the 78th minute before Mastantuono completed the rout in the 88th minute, connecting with Giuliano Simeone’s pass. The result gave Argentina a seven-goal victory, with three players scoring twice as they overwhelmed Costa Rica. The victory came after Argentina lost 2-1 to Uruguay in their first match following Lionel Messi’s farewell to international football in October. Messi played his final game for Argentina in a 3-0 friendly victory over Benin on October 6, bringing an end to his international career with the national team.
